storage.intro: A pool combines disks into one storage space protected by RAID. Below: every disk and its health (SMART).
storage.unavailable: Disks cannot be read on this system. Storage Manager needs Linux with lsblk and smartctl.

smart.failedHelp: This disk reports that it is about to fail. Back up the data on it now, then replace the disk.
smart.warningHelp: This disk shows early signs of failure, such as bad or reallocated sectors. Data is still readable: back it up now and plan to replace the disk.
smart.standbyHelp: The disk is in power-saving mode. SMART is not read so the disk is not woken up; try again later.
smart.unsupportedHelp: This disk does not provide health data (common for virtual disks and some USB adapters).
smart.failingNote: Attributes marked red have crossed the manufacturer's threshold.
smart.warningNote: Attributes marked yellow have a non-zero value on a monitored damage counter.

https.title: The panel uses a secure connection
https.intro: The Sapo panel only opens over HTTPS so your password and data are encrypted on the network.
https.step1: Click the button below. Your browser will show a certificate warning because this certificate was created by the NAS itself, not by a certificate authority.
https.step2: Open the certificate details in that warning and make sure its SHA-256 fingerprint matches the one shown on the NAS screen (console login screen).
https.step3: If it matches, proceed to the site. This warning appears only once for this browser.
https.fingerprint: Certificate fingerprint (SHA-256). For convenience only: this page is not encrypted yet, so the trusted value is the one shown on the NAS screen.
https.why: If the fingerprint in your browser differs from the one on the NAS screen, do not proceed: another device may be impersonating your NAS. From now on, open the panel directly with its https:// address.

pool.title: Storage pools
pool.created: Pool {name} has been created and is ready to use.
pool.unavailable: Pools can’t be read on this system.
pool.zfsMissing: ZFS isn’t ready on this NAS, so pools can’t be created yet. Install the ZFS storage feature, then restart the NAS.
pool.none: No pools yet. Create a pool to start storing data.
pool.noneNoDisks: No pools yet, and no disk is available. Add a disk to create a pool.

health.degradedHelp: A disk has failed or is missing. Your data is still intact, but protection is reduced: replace the failing disk as soon as possible.
health.faultedHelp: The pool can’t be used. Don’t erase or format any disk; check the disk connections and the ZFS message below.

pool.almostFull: The pool is almost full. Above 80% ZFS slows down; delete data or add capacity.

scan.never: Never scrubbed. A scrub reads all data and repairs damage from healthy copies.

single.name: Single disk (no RAID)
single.desc: All capacity is usable, but if the disk fails all data is lost.

mirror.name: Mirror (RAID 1)
mirror.desc: Every disk holds the same copy. Simplest, and quickest to rebuild.

raidz1.name: RAID-Z1 (like RAID 5)
raidz1.desc: One disk’s worth of capacity is used for parity.

raidz2.name: RAID-Z2 (like RAID 6)
raidz2.desc: Two disks’ worth of capacity for parity. Recommended for large disks.

raidz3.name: RAID-Z3
raidz3.desc: Three disks’ worth of capacity for parity, for pools with many disks.

pool.tolerates: no disk can fail | 1 disk can fail | {n} disks can fail
pool.mixedSizes: The disks differ in size. Each disk is only used up to the smallest one ({size}).
pool.eraseWarning: All data on these disks will be permanently erased:
pool.pickLayout: Choose a layout that fits the number of disks.
pool.replaced: The disk is being replaced. ZFS is rebuilding data onto the new disk (resilver); the pool stays usable meanwhile.
